[[File:Brigitte Sarry.jpg|alt=Picture of Brigitte Sarry|thumb|Brigitte Sarry]]
'''Brigitte Sarry''' (6 September 1920 in Allenstein – 19 June 2017 in Berlin) was a German chemist and a professor at [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Müller|first=Jörn|date=2017|title=Brigitte Sarry (1920 – 2017)|journal=Nachrichten aus der Chemie|language=en|volume=65|issue=10|pages=1047|doi=10.1002/nadc.20174067201|issn=1868-0054}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archiv.pressestelle.tu-berlin.de/pi/2001/pi19.htm|title=TU Berlin - Medieninformation Nr. 19 - 26. Januar 2001|website=archiv.pressestelle.tu-berlin.de|access-date=2019-01-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://trauer.tagesspiegel.de/traueranzeige/brigitte-sarry|title=Gedenkseite von Brigitte Sarry|website=trauer.tagesspiegel.de|language=de|access-date=2019-01-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Geschichte der anorganischen Chemie: Die Entwicklung einer Wissenschaft in Deutschland von Döbereiner bis heute|last=Werner|first=Helmut|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2016|isbn=9783527693009|location=Weinheim, Germany|pages=181–182|oclc=964358572}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chemie.tu-berlin.de/menue/institut_fuer_chemie/wichtigetermineweiteres_seiten_teilweise/nachruf_brigitte_sarry/|title=Institut für Chemie: Nachruf Brigitte Sarry|website=www.chemie.tu-berlin.de|access-date=2019-01-13}}</ref>

== Life ==
Sarry grew up in Allenstein.<ref name=":0" /> After moving with her family to Göttingen, she finished her Abitur in Göttingen in 1939.<ref name=":0" /> Sarry studied chemistry at the [[University of Göttingen]], interrupted by an interlude at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]].<ref name=":0" /> She wrote her diploma thesis as well as her dissertation in the working group of [[Günther Rienäcker]] on para-hydrogen conversions on solid solutions of copper and platinum. She started her dissertation in Göttingen and finished it later at the [[University of Rostock]].<ref name=":0" /> Brigitte Sarry received her doctorate in Rostock on the 14th of April in 1945.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cpr.uni-rostock.de/resolve/id/cpr_person_00002665|title=Sarry, Brigitte - Catalogus Professorum Rostochiensium|website=cpr.uni-rostock.de|access-date=2019-01-13}}</ref> In 1954, she finished her habilitation in Inorganic Chemistry at the University of Rostock.<ref name=":0" /> This habilitation focused on the investigation of hydrogen compounds of transition metals.<ref name=":0" /> Sarry declined a professorship [[Technische Hochschule Leuna-Merseburg]], did research at the [[University of Stuttgart]], and then worked as a lecturer at the [[University of Halle]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1958, Brigitte Sarry fled to West Berlin, where she continued her scientific research under difficult external conditions at today's [[TU Berlin]].<ref name=":0" /> She started as a "wissenschaftliche Rätin" and then worked as an extraordinary professor.<ref name=":0" /> In March 1969, Sarry was appointed full professor at TU Berlin.<ref name=":0" /> She worked there at the Institute of Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry in the field of organometallic compounds of transition elements, and she provided important impulses for the development of homoleptic metal organyls.<ref name=":0" /> In autumn 1982, Brigitte Sarry retired early for health reasons.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
One of her research topics were homoleptic metal organyls.<ref name=":0" /> She was also able to isolate and characterize [[pyrophoricity|pyrophoric]] and thermically unstable solids such as Li<sub>4</sub>Ta(C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>6</sub> ∙ 3.5 O(C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>2</sub> and Li<sub>3</sub>Mo(''p''-C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Me)<sub>6</sub> ∙ 3 O(C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>2</sub>.<ref name=":1" />

== Publications ==
Sarry published the following textbook on general chemistry:

* {{Cite book|title=Eigenschaften und Bau der Atome|last=Sarry|first=Brigitte|publisher=Urania|year=1956|isbn=|location=|pages=|asin=B00709UCES |asin-tld=de}}

She also updated and extended a German translation of a textbook on inorganic chemistry: 
*{{Cite book|title=Anorganische Chemie: Prinzipien von Struktur und Reaktivität|last1=Huheey|first1=James E.|last2=Reuter|first2=Bertold|last3=Sarry|first3=Brigitte|date=1988|publisher=De Gruyter|isbn=978-3110081633|location=Berlin|pages=|oclc=46194314}}
